name: HDC2080DMBR
title: Low-power digital relative humidity and temperature sensor with I2C interface
summary: The HDC2080 measures relative humidity with a capacitive polymer element and temperature with an on-chip sensor, converts both with an ADC against factory calibration, and reports them over I2C. It runs from 1.62 V to 3.6 V and idles at 50 nA typical; it can sample on command or on its own at one of seven rates, raise a data-ready or threshold interrupt on DRDY/INT, and warm itself with a built-in heater to drive off condensation. It comes in a 3 mm by 3 mm 6-pin WSON with the sensing opening on top.
key_figures: 0.3 µA (RH or temperature only), 0.55 µA (RH + temperature, 11 bit)
I2C, 10 kHz to 400 kHz, two addresses

circuits.title: Typical application
circuits.description: The sensor shares a 1.80 V rail with a microcontroller acting as I2C master. SCL and SDA each have a pull-up resistor to the rail; DRDY/INT goes to a GPIO of the MCU so it can sleep until data is ready or a threshold trips. ADDR is tied to ground, selecting address 0x40.
notes: A 0.1 µF X7R ceramic capacitor between VDD and GND is recommended.

circuits.title: Battery-powered HVAC thermostat
circuits.description: A thermostat runs from a lithium-ion cell on a 1.8 V rail that feeds the sensor, the MCU and the display. The MCU reads humidity and temperature over I2C, with one pull-up resistor each on SCL and SDA to the rail, and takes the sensor's interrupt on a GPIO. ADDR is grounded. Further MCU GPIOs drive the display and scan a four-button keypad.
notes: Misprint: the sensor in this figure is marked HDC2010; it should read HDC2080.
The display and keypad links are multi-wire GPIO buses.

operation.text: A polymer dielectric forms a capacitive humidity element; a separate on-chip sensor measures temperature. Both go through an ADC and are corrected with factory calibration coefficients. Each channel can be set to 9, 11 or 14 bit, and the conversion time depends on the resolution chosen.

At power-up the device sits in sleep mode, drawing 50 nA typical, until an I2C command arrives. A triggered measurement switches it to measurement mode, writes the results to the data registers and then returns it to sleep.

operation.topic: Trigger on demand and auto measurement
operation.text: In trigger-on-demand use each conversion is started by setting MEAS_TRIG over I2C. In auto measurement mode the AMM field of register 0x0E picks one of seven rates, from one sample every 2 minutes to 5 samples per second, and the device wakes and converts on its own, so the host can stay asleep.
After power is applied the sensor is ready to start measuring within 3 ms at most; it stays in sleep until addressed.

Setting HEAT_EN turns on an internal heater, which can clear condensation or check the temperature sensor. It draws 90 mA typical at 3.3 V and 55 mA at 1.8 V, and while it is on the device temperature must stay below 85 °C. One way to use it: track the dew point in firmware, switch the heater on when condensation is likely, keep measuring until RH reads near zero, then switch off and let the part cool, which can take minutes, before trusting readings again. Heating evaporates water on the sensor but leaves any dissolved contaminants behind, and their residue can affect humidity accuracy.

The pin is high impedance until DRDY/INT_EN (0x0E bit 2) is set. INT_POL chooses active-high or active-low. With DRDY_ENABLE set, DRDY_STATUS goes to 1 when a conversion finishes and the pin follows it; for the data-ready function INT_MODE is to be 0. The pin shows only one enabled source at a time, not an OR of them: TH_ENABLE has priority over TL_ENABLE, then HH_ENABLE, then HL_ENABLE.

Each threshold (temperature high and low, humidity high and low) sets its status bit when the reading passes its threshold register. With INT_MODE = 0 the status bit and pin latch until the status register is read; with INT_MODE = 1 (comparator) they follow each new conversion. Reading register 0x04 clears the threshold bits; DRDY_STATUS also clears when the four result registers are read.
ADDR selects 1000000 (low or open) or 1000001 (high), so two sensors can share a bus. Set ADDR before any bus traffic and keep it fixed while powered.

The device is a target only. SDA and SCL have spike filters and Schmitt-trigger inputs. Bytes go MSB first. A write sends the register address after the address byte and then data; a read first writes the register pointer, then repeats START with the read bit. The pointer increments automatically for multi-byte transfers. Writing a read-only ID register NACKs each data byte; an unused register address NACKs after the pointer; a wrong device address NACKs at once.

Temperature and humidity are each 16-bit results whose two lowest bits are always 0; the conversion is always 14 bit and the resolution setting decides how many bits are meaningful. Read the low byte first.
TEMPERATURE MAX and HUMIDITY MAX keep the highest values converted since power-up; power cycling or a soft reset clears them. They do not work in auto measurement mode.
TEMP_OFFSET_ADJUST and HUM_OFFSET_ADJUST hold a signed offset, built from the bit weights in their tables, that is added to every converted result.
The manufacturer ID reads 0x4954 (registers 0xFD:0xFC) and the device ID 0x07D0 (0xFF:0xFE).
Writing 1 to SOFT_RES reloads the EEPROM values and returns the registers to reset; the bit clears itself.
Supply 1.62 V to 3.60 V, with a 0.1 µF X7R multilayer ceramic capacitor between VDD and GND.

Keep the sensor away from heat sources such as active circuits, batteries, displays and resistors; where space is short, cut-outs or trenches in the board around it reduce heat flow. Sample at 1 Hz at most to avoid self-heating. Openings in the product enclosure let the air at the sensor match the room even in still conditions.

The humidity element faces up through an opening in the top of the package. Remove the GND and VDD copper under the device and slot the board around it for thermal isolation, and use the land pattern, solder mask and paste openings of the package drawings. Only the bypass capacitor sits next to the sensor. The exposed pad can be soldered to an unconnected board pad, which is not to be connected to GND.
Avoid long exposure to UV or visible light and to chemical vapours, including solvents outgassed by adhesive tapes, stickers, bubble wrap and other packaging, during manufacture, transport and use.

Standard reflow to IPC/JEDEC J-STD-020 with a 260 °C peak. No-clean paste is required and the board must not be rinsed with water or solvents. After reflow the RH reading is offset; it returns to calibrated accuracy after several days at room temperature in 30 % to 40 %RH.

One reflow with no rework is preferred. A second pass through reflow can be tolerated when the exposed polymer stays clean and undamaged, no-clean paste is used without any liquid exposure, and the peak stays at or below 260 °C.

Best accuracy is kept within 20 % to 80 %RH, non-condensing, from 0 °C to 70 °C. Long periods beyond that, worst at high RH together with high temperature, can offset the reading and recovery is slow.
To recover from a lasting offset after harsh exposure or contamination: bake at 100 °C below 5 %RH for 5 to 10 hours, then re-hydrate at 20 °C to 30 °C and 60 % to 75 %RH for 6 to 12 hours.
